lesson.title: Niño or Niña? A Picture Sorting Game
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol brought a big pile of pictures today — some show boys, some show girls. Let's sort them into two groups with Sol!
A boy is [[el niño]] in Spanish. Find a picture of a boy — a class photo or a storybook character — and say '¡Es el niño!'
A girl is [[la niña]] in Spanish. Find a picture of a girl and say '¡Es la niña!'
You sorted pictures into el niño and la niña piles — great listening! Tomorrow, you'll introduce a friend to Sol.

objectives: Say el niño (boy) when shown a picture of a boy
Say la niña (girl) when shown a picture of a girl
materialsNeeded: A pile of pictures with people in them — class photos, family photos, or storybook illustrations work well
Two spots on the floor or table to sort pictures into
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Lay out a small pile of pictures showing children — mix boys and girls, from photos or storybooks.
2. Hold up a picture of a boy and say '¡Es el niño!' — coach your child to echo el niño and place it in the 'niño' pile.
3. Hold up a picture of a girl and say '¡Es la niña!' — coach your child to echo la niña and place it in the 'niña' pile.
4. Mix up the pictures and let your child sort 4-5 more on their own, saying el niño or la niña for each before placing it.
5. Point to yourself or a family member and ask: '¿Eres el niño o la niña?' (Are you the boy or the girl?) and answer together.
6. Close by asking your child: 'What do we call a boy in Spanish? What do we call a girl?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: sort just 3-4 very clear pictures at first, and say the word for your child to echo before they try it alone
Ready for more: add stuffed animals or toy figures dressed as characters and sort those too, describing why each one is el niño or la niña
This is a listening-and-sorting activity — your child never needs to read the words el niño or la niña to learn them
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken sorting activity — success looks like your child saying el niño for pictures of boys and la niña for pictures of girls as they sort, not a written answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Extends week 2's WA-WL-2015.1.1 target with the vocabulary needed to talk about the other people in a name-and-friends conversation, taught through a hands-on picture sort rather than direct instruction, matching this band's oral/aural-first design.

worksheet.title: Niño or Niña? A Picture Sorting Game

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and sort pictures together — there's nothing for your child to write today.

rows.problem: Gather 4-6 pictures showing children, from photos or storybooks.
Hold up a picture of a boy. Say '¡Es el niño!' together and set it in one pile.
Hold up a picture of a girl. Say '¡Es la niña!' together and set it in a second pile.
Mix up the rest and let your child sort them, saying el niño or la niña each time.
